help.title: Help
help.about.b: PathShrink shortens the paths that OneDrive and SharePoint cannot sync because they are over 400 characters. It does it by renaming folders: first it removes surplus spaces, then it joins words, and only if you allow it, it removes letters from the end of the longest folder names. It does not delete, move or open any file: every file stays in its folder with the same content. What changes is the name of some folders, and of files only if you allow it and no folder can give more.
help.longPath.b: A path whose length, counted the way OneDrive and SharePoint count it, is over the target (the limit minus the safety margin). Over 400 characters it does not sync at all.
help.pathLength.b: Characters of the path on the server: the library address (for example personal/ana_perez_contoso_com/Documents/), every folder, every separator and the file name. It is longer than the path you see in File Explorer.
help.scan.b: Reads the names of the files and folders in the chosen folder and measures every path. It only reads names: it does not open files, does not download cloud-only files and changes nothing.
help.plan.b: The exact list of renames PathShrink proposes: current name, new name, why it is needed and which paths it fixes. Nothing happens until you apply it. In Pro mode you can leave out single renames.
help.dryRun.b: While you look at the analysis and the plan, nothing has been changed on disk. It is the same as -WhatIf on the command line. Changes only happen after Apply and your confirmation.
help.apply.b: Renames the items in the plan, deepest first. Each rename is written to undo.csv the moment it happens; afterwards the folder is read again to check the result.
help.revert.b: Gives each item back the name it had, using the undo.csv of that run. Every item is checked first: if it was moved, renamed again or deleted, or something else now uses the old name, it is skipped and listed. Nothing is overwritten. Only names change back; contents were never touched.
help.report.b: A folder with report.html (every long path, before and after, with the changed names highlighted), paths.csv, planned-renames.csv and summary.json. After applying it also holds renames.csv, undo.csv and run.json.
help.clean.b: Removes double spaces, spaces around - _ , and spaces or dots at the end of a name. No letter is lost.
help.join.b: Removes the spaces between words and capitalises each word: "Tax returns" becomes "TaxReturns". No letter is lost. Names in capitals go last, because without spaces they are hard to read.
help.trim.b: Optional. Removes letters from the end of the longest folder names, one at a time and spread over several folders, never below the shortest name you set. Only the folder name changes: its files, their content and their location stay the same. File names are shortened only if no folder can give more, and they keep their extension.
help.limit.b: The longest path allowed, in characters. OneDrive and SharePoint Online: 400. Change it only for another system with a lower limit.
help.margin.b: Paths this close to the limit are shortened too, so that the next file with a slightly longer name does not fail again. Default 20, so the target is 400 - 20 = 380.
help.minName.b: When names are shortened, none is cut below this number of characters. Default 20.
help.exclude.b: Wildcards for folders or files that are neither analysed nor renamed, for example Archive* or Clients\Old*.
help.protect.b: Wildcards for names that count towards the length but are never renamed, for example client codes such as CLIENT*.
help.prefix.b: The library address OneDrive puts in front of every path, for example sites/Legal/Shared Documents/. It is read from the OneDrive client; enter it by hand only to analyse a copied folder.
help.limits.b: A rename breaks shortcuts, pins and copied links that point inside the renamed folder (reverting fixes them). Other people see the new names once OneDrive syncs. If someone changes an item after the run, that item cannot be reverted automatically. Paths nested too deep may not fit without moving folders, which PathShrink never does.
